question: Abdul and Mohsin together invested ₹79,200 in a business. At the end of the year, out of a total profit of ₹14,400, Mohsin's share was ₹2,600. What was the difference between their investments?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Profit** = Ratio of **Investment** (since time period is same).

Total Profit = ₹14,400 | **Mohsin share** = ₹2,600 | **Abdul share** = 14,400 − 2,600 = ₹11,800.

Investment Ratio (Abdul : Mohsin) = 11,800 : 2,600 = 118 : 26 = 59 : 13.

Difference in ratio parts = 59 − 13 = 46 units | Total parts = 59 + 13 = 72 units.

Value of 46 units = (Total Investment ÷ 72) × 46 = (79,200 ÷ 72) × 46 = 1,100 × 46 = ₹50,600.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹50,600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → Total Investment = ₹79,200 | Total Profit = ₹14,400 | Mohsin Profit = ₹2,600.
Formulas → Profit Ratio = Investment Ratio (for same time) | ProfitA = Total Profit − ProfitM | Difference = InvestmentA − InvestmentM.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2588011d22ab7a7f1c95ae1ce288656cd4253cd13d887c4fd21c5b1a9e373b5e.png] 
⇒ Abdul Profit = 14,400 − 2,600 = ₹11,800.
⇒ Investment Ratio (Abdul : Mohsin) = 11,800 : 2,600 = 59 : 13.
⇒ Let Abdul investment be 59x and Mohsin be 13x.
⇒ 59x + 13x = 79,200 ⇒ 72x = 79,200 ⇒ x = 1,100.
⇒ Difference = 59x − 13x = 46x = 46 × 1,100 = ₹50,600.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹50,600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Partnership Basics

When time periods are equal, the **ratio of profits** is directly proportional to the **ratio of capitals** (investments) invested by partners.

Variable Time Partnership

If time periods are different, Profit Ratio = (Capital₁ × Time₁) : (Capital₂ × Time₂).
